name: 116. Session affinity matrix on Vertex and Anthropic (session-affinity)
description:
Wire-level pins for session affinity across every lever that can change where a session lands: what makes a request take part (x-bf-session-id, the Claude Code and Codex session headers, x-bf-session-affinity: off, a provider-prefixed model), what builds the chain the session reorders (routing rules with targets, pins and fallbacks, a real upstream failure that moves the session to a fallback, a one-provider chain that drops a binding), what pins outrank the session's key binding (a rule's pin changed mid-session), and what governance takes away (a virtual key whose key_ids no longer include the bound key). It also pins that a streamed request binds and follows a session like any other (case 14), that a binding lasts only as long as the x-bf-session-ttl it was written with (case 15), that a request pinned to the caller's own key does not rebind the session (case 16), that a Claude Code session on /anthropic/v1/messages is followed the same way (case 17), and that two virtual keys sending one session id keep separate bindings (case 18). Every sequence uses one fresh session id and asserts extra_fields.provider, routing_info.key and routing_info.is_fallback. Streamed rows read the same three facts from the x-bifrost-routing-info-* headers.

Static rules live in tests/integrations/python/config.json (governance.routing_rules) behind the harness-only header x-harness-session-pin: bind, vertex, rebind, rescue, vertex-only, anthropic-first, anthropic-first-other-model and vertex-badkey. Two of them pin keys that cannot serve the model on purpose: the rescue rule's Anthropic fallback (so the promoted Anthropic attempt fails on the same model, which exact route matching requires) and the vertex-badkey rule (so a request fails at key selection without leaving the bound route). Case 12 pins that a binding names provider and model together, and case 13 that a binding followed into a failure is forgotten. Cases 9, 10, 11 and 18 are single rows that do their own management work through pm.sendRequest: for 9 to 11 the pre-request script creates a second Anthropic key from the same env credential, a run-scoped routing rule keyed by x-harness-session-run, and for case 11 a virtual key; for 18 it creates two virtual keys and binds the session under the first. The test script makes the follow-up inference call with the same session id and deletes everything it created. One row per case is deliberate: the recipe forks a newman process per provider and per modality class and sub-shards a class by row position, and collection variables never cross a process, so state set up in one row cannot be consumed in another. Leftovers of an aborted run carry their run timestamp in their names and are swept by the next run once they are ten minutes old; younger objects belong to a shard that may still be running. The whole folder is attributed to the Vertex fork.
